why_null: All four cases in the library were considered and none matched at the motif level. B-01 (casualty-inflation cascade, May 2019) and B-03 (moral-shock acceleration, Aug 2025) both run on a moral shock carried by a count or an image that mobilizes before any correction can travel; the mbg-stop family carries no such shock, and its engine is an arithmetic step from one budget line to the whole budget. B-02 (fabricated-provision cascade, Oct 2020) turns on provisions attributed to a legal text whose final wording was not yet public, and nothing in this family attributes invented content to any document: the amounts it carries resolve to registry entries, and the weakness sits in the steps between them rather than in the figures themselves. B-04 (scope-inflation panic, Jan 2025) is the nearest case in the library and still not the same shape. There, a measure drafted narrow in a ministerial regulation was retold as covering the whole consumption basket, a mismatch between the scope of a rule as written and the scope as retold. The motif here is different: a single lever priced as sufficient for a system-wide result, with the total it would have to be measured against left unstated, and with spending already disbursed treated as still recoverable. Shared fiscal subject matter is topic, not structure, and the library holds no documented episode whose shape is the single-lever sufficiency step. The Echo section stays silent, which the blueprint permits explicitly.
